meaningMnemonic: This radical is made of dirt, legs, and winter. If you have to bury your legs in the dirt in winter, it's probably because you got frostbite . You had to leave your dead legs behind. :(

If you point a bunch of flowers in the same direction , you'll be able to smell their aromatic fragrance . The best way to bask in their fragrance is to make them all point in the same direction (preferably straight at you). Hints Imagine aiming a bunch of flowers in the same direction towards you. Their aromatic fragrance coats your body. You smell great now!
readingMnemonic: You decide to bring this aromatic fragrance into your ho me ( ほう ). To do this, you plant flowers all the way around your home, all facing in toward it. Hints Unfortunately, now when you're at home you're choked by the overwhelming fragrance of flowers, all concentrating their aromas on a single point (your home). Oh… oh no it's too strong. You can't breathe. And you live alone. Help! Someone!

meaningMnemonic: When a spirit lives in a sheep it becomes the most auspicious creature on the planet. Lights shine out of it and the whole world weeps at its beauty. Look at the sheep's fluffy glowing head. Nothing could be more auspicious and glorious than this. Hints Picture this auspicious spirit sheep. Blessing the children with its fluffy hooves.
readingMnemonic: The spirit sheep is so auspicious that the Shou gun ( しょう ) declares this day to be the most auspicious of all days. The day when the spirit sheep appeared. Hints Picture the Shougun telling the world that they must fly spirit sheep flags on this day forever, because of how auspicious it is.

meaningMnemonic: I hope all you're doing in the bathtub is taking a bath . I mean, you can do other things if you want I guess. But bathtubs were made just for baths! Hints Picture yourself taking a bath in your bathtub. Relaxing!
readingMnemonic: When do you miss taking a bath the most? When you're on the ro ad ( ろ ). Traveling is fun and all, but when you're stuck in a car, traveling down a dirt road for days, all you want to do is take a nice long bath. Hints Imagine being stuck on the road all day for a week. Imagine how good a bath will feel when you finally get home. Nice and hot and relaxing. Mmmm...

meaningMnemonic: The leader of the library thinks that all the books in their library are better than everyone else's books. He's a very biased person. If he wasn't the leader of that specific library he'd probably feel differently. Hints Imagine showing the leader your favorite book. "That's not a book in MY library," he says, and throws it in the trash. That's so biased! He didn't even give it a shot!
readingMnemonic: You decide to give in to his biased recommendations and look at what he has in his library. It doesn't take long until you realize that these books are all about hen s ( へん ) and hen care. This guy is so biased about his favorite books that he only filled his library with what HE wants to read. And apparently that thing is taking care of hens... weird. Hints "This is such biased crap," you say, as you finish reading the title of a book called "Hens are better than all other birds." Screw this leader guy and his books.

meaningMnemonic: If you look at flowers the first thing you notice are the leaves and petals themselves, then the next thing you notice are the briar s. You never see thorn s first, only after you've looked at the flowers. Hints Imagine what you see next after looking at the pretty flowers. The briars are what you see next. Spiky and sharp. It would have been nice if you had seen them first.
readingMnemonic: When you see the briar s you can't help but yell, Eee! Ba riars ! ( いばら )! You sound funny because you prick your finger on one while you're yelling. Ouch! Hints Imagine seeing the briars and yelling out "Ba RI ars!" as you prick your finger on one.

meaningMnemonic: This building was a former prison until the cave in . You see, prisons aren't built very carefully, they just try to get them done fast enough to stuff people in there. So while you can tell this was once a building, it definitely isn't a prison anymore, since the whole thing caved in. Hints Picture the cave in in your mind. Can you see all the little prisoners and guards being squished as the building tumbles down around them? Oh no!
readingMnemonic: You keep picturing the cave in and you see Genghis Khan ( かん ) climbing over the rubble. He's the one who took down this prison! And he's coming for your town next! Hints Genghis Khan is all about being smart and using better tactics. In this case, why fight a bunch of guards and prisoners when you can just cause a cave in and win immediately? The ol' Khan cave in, a classic war maneuver.

meaningMnemonic: The famous gold triceratops shellfish is good for only one thing, and that's being made into chain s. They link their triceratops horns together and form an unbreakable gold chain. You can't eat them, because they're gold. So they're only really good for their chaining together ability. Hints Picture these little gold triceratops shellfish linked together by their horns in a chain around your neck. Feel them hanging there. Sparkly and cold.
readingMnemonic: However, the only way to break the chain is to cut it open with a saw ( さ ). Once the golden triceratops shellfish start holding on, they never let go. So when you want to take the chain off you have to really hack at it with your saw. Hints Picture the saw in your hands, sawing back and forth on the gold chain around your neck. Maybe this isn't the best fashion accessory if you have to use a saw to get it off.

meaningMnemonic: You give a bunch of shellfish to a clown as compensation . The clown did you some favors, and everyone knows clowns only accept shellfish as a form of currency. So your compensation is a pile of random shellfish. Hints Picture the shellfish in your hands. Imagine handing them over to the clown as compensation for the unspeakable acts you had him do for you.
readingMnemonic: Once the clown has been properly compensate d, he looks you in the eyes, one hand full of shellfish, the other in the air, and waves, " Bye ( ばい )" he says. "Bye, bye." Hints All you have to do is give him the right amount of compensation and you'll hear his sweet "bye, bye." Then you never have to see him again.

meaningMnemonic: Your soul is like the ground or the dawn . It is constant , never changing. Hints Think of some other things your soul is like, but always make sure you come back to one word: constant.
readingMnemonic: Also constant is the Emperor こう いち , who will surely rule for a thousand more years! Hints A constant rule from Emperor こういち means constant kanji learning and constant WaniKani reviews. They will always be constant!

meaningMnemonic: You're sewing something with thread but you and your creation get frostbite while you're still working. Luckily the snowflakes freeze themselves into the cloth and turn into a pretty design . They swirl around and press a unique snowy design into the fabric. This is nice for you because you can't sew anymore with your frostbitten hands. Hints Imagine holding your creation in your frostbitten hands as the snowflake design starts to appear. The design gets more and more complicated the longer you watch, twisting this way and that, like it's dancing in front of your eyes.
readingMnemonic: As you watch the snowflake design form you see letters appearing in the corner! They form the name Aya ( あや ), our artist here at WaniKani. Somehow she's magically putting together this beautiful pattern! Hints If you know someone else called Aya, go ahead and use them in this mnemonic! Whoever it is, imagine an Aya watching from afar holding a magic wand, creating this beautiful frosty pattern!

meaningMnemonic: If you figure out how to use a tsunami as a weapon , everyone is going to die . You can't control a tsunami, you fool. Now you've doomed us all. Hints Picture everyone in the world being swept away in a tsunami to die. This is what happens when you try to use nature as a weapon.
readingMnemonic: The only way to maybe not die is to find boats ( ぼつ ). As long as the boats don't get smashed by the tsunami, you might be able to cheat death by holding onto the boats and not drowning. Hints You don't want to die, do you? Get to the boats!

meaningMnemonic: Your fingers grasp this lid and when you raise it you see a poop turkey (a turkey covered in poop). You can't help yourself, you embrace the turkey. Hints Someone was obviously going to cook this poop turkey in a pot, and if you hadn't looked under this lid it surely would have died. Now as you embrace it you can hear the turkey weeping softly.
readingMnemonic: As you embrace the sad turkey it makes a funny sound and suddenly starts pooping yo gurt ( よう ) all over you. But you don't want to stop embracing it! It's probably just scared still. But the more you squeeze, the faster the yogurt comes out of it! Hints Imagine embracing the turkey as it covers you in yogurt poo. You hope it's yogurt at least. You aren't gonna taste it to find out. Maybe. Okay you might taste it a little.

meaningMnemonic: When you ride your scooter on the ground listening to music under the sun , you're bound to encounter a bunch of new people! They hear your music playing as you scoot by and they come out to meet you. Hints Picture all of the people you encounter as you ride your scooter, spreading your music around town.
readingMnemonic: Everyone you encounter wants to bare their sou l ( そう ) to you, literally. They're all coming out to meet you, pulling back their skin and showing you the soul ghosts inside of them. Hints "We love your music, look at our souls!" Uh oh, this is turning into some kind of horror movie. You better scoot a bit faster or you might meet an unfortunate fate.

meaningMnemonic: From your mouth comes a cross , some flowers , and shellfish . It all erupt s from your mouth! Hints Imagine these three things coming out of your mouth not one at a time, but all together like an eruption. Perhaps you're laying on your back, and they burst out of your mouth.
readingMnemonic: When do inanimate objects erupt from your mouth? Mostly when you're having fun ( ふん ). Hints It's really inconvenient that things erupt from your mouth whenever you're having fun. Makes it hard to have fun. Fun fact: when you see 賁 in a kanji, the reading is probably going to be ふん .

meaningMnemonic: Within the yakuza , having a slide on your jet means you're especially important and powerful. It's a symbol of how especially awesome and badass you are. Hints A jet with a teeter-totter? Normal yakuza boss. A jet with a jungle gym? Powerful yakuza boss. A jet with a slide? Especially powerful yakuza boss.
readingMnemonic: These especially powerful yakuza bosses have slides that are like chu tes ( しゅ ) — they're especially fast and especially fun! Hints Just don't get on the bad side of one of these especially important yakuza bosses — a trap door at the bottom of the chute will open and drop you out of their jet.

meaningMnemonic: A leader puts their hat on the ground next to a bookshelf . This is a test in ethics . Hints People hang around the bookshelf, and the leader wants to see if anyone will steal the hat or not. That's why its a test of ethics.
readingMnemonic: To test your ethics even more, the leader puts down a rin g ( りん ) as well. Hints Now we'll really see how everyone's ethics are. Will they turn in the ring to the lost and found? Will they ignore it? Will they steal it?

meaningMnemonic: The building to the east is an exhibit . Hints It's a pretty large building and you can see inside to all of the different exhibits within the main exhibit.
readingMnemonic: Right now the exhibit has a bunch of chin s ( ちん ) on display. Animal chins, human chins, every chin you can think of is in the exhibit. Hints Go up to the first exhibit and look very closely at some turtle chins, then some crab chins, then some alligator chins. This is weirdly familiar.

meaningMnemonic: If you tie a cross to a turkey you can trick everyone into thinking it's a falcon . The cross will stretch its wings out just enough for it to stop looking so fat and turkey like, into a super cool bird of prey. Hints Imagine tying a cross to this turkey and see it transform into an elegant falcon. Majestic.
readingMnemonic: You decide to name this new falcon after your favorite falcon-like ninja. Ryu Hayabusa ( はやぶさ ) from Ninja Gaiden ! Picture your fat turkey falcon and Ryu Hayabusa teaming up Banjo and Kazooey style. Yeah, that's the dream right there. Hints Picture your falcon Hayabusa and the real... ok fake.. Hayabusa running around together and kicking butt.

meaningMnemonic: What do stairs do? They take you from where you were, to somewhere else. They're a way to get from place to place. Hints Picture yourself climbing stairs, picture going from room to room. From place to place. From wherever you were to wherever you want to be.
readingMnemonic: If you're going from place to place, make sure you have some no ri ( の ) seaweed on you, in case you get hungry. Nori is a great source of energy. Hints Imagine yourself going from one place to another with your pockets stuffed full of nori. The smell is starting to get overwhelming. It's making you really hungry (or nauseous, depending on how you feel about nori!).

meaningMnemonic: If you want to have your wedding in a car you're going to need a lot of help . Cars are pretty small compared to weddings, so if you don't get help from everyone you know you won't be able to pull it off. Hints Picture all of your close friends coming to help you squeeze everything for the wedding into your car.
readingMnemonic: You can't just ask for help on the day of the wedding, either. You have to sche dule ( すけ ) getting your friends' help ahead of time. They might have pretty tight schedules too, so make sure you plan early! Hints Imagine calling all your friends and scheduling when you will get their help. Make sure you have your day planner ready!

meaningMnemonic: There is an animal in the grass and your horrible task is to go hunting for it. Hints Picture the shape of the animal in the grass, off in the distance. You can't see what kind of animal it is yet, but you know you're hunting it.
readingMnemonic: You're currently hunting in a row ( りょう ) boat and you have to row as quietly and carefully as you can or the animal will run away. Hints You wouldn't be able to go hunting in any other kind of boat—the motor would be too loud. Picture yourself in a row boat with all of your hunting gear. You need to be extra careful not to make any loud splashing sounds with the oars!

meaningMnemonic: Beside your mouth is an evil spider that tries to instigate you into saying bad things and starting a riot. It's like the little silken puppet master of your mouth or something. Don't let it instigate you! Hints Imagine this spider controlling your mouth with its web, making you say things you wouldn't dare think of. "Free healthcare for all!" "Pineapple is a legitimate pizza topping!" Man, you gotta stop letting that spider instigate you into saying weird stuff.
readingMnemonic: You want the spider to stop instigating you into saying bad things and starting riots. So you pick up a saw ( さ ) and start cutting off the silken threads that are controlling your mouth. Hints If this spider's web is strong enough to control your mouth, you will most likely need a saw to cut it off, right?

meaningMnemonic: If you give a machine a heart it will get lazy and neglect its duties. Hearts give us emotions and with emotions we become weak. Why would a machine with a heart want to work anymore? Nah. It's going to be lazy and neglectful now. Hints Picture a machine with a heart, lying on the couch, eating oil snacks, snoozing and neglecting the orders you've given it. What a lazy machine!
readingMnemonic: The machine is so lazy it even starts to neglect its tie ( たい ). It's supposed to wear one, but it's too lazy to put it on now. Do lazy humans put on ties? Nope, and neither do neglectful machines. Hints Picture this lazy machine sitting on the couch again. There are untied ties all over the floor, hanging on the back of the couch, but it totally neglects them.

meaningMnemonic: In its soul , a narwhal that's supposed to do construction under the moon will be too lazy to do it. And when your soul is lazy, there's no way you'll be able to get something done. Hints Picture the lazy narwhal lounging around under the moonlight. He's got all his construction tools spread out around him, but he just can't seem to get up and do any work.
readingMnemonic: You can't tell the lazy narwhal he's being lazy because he's your da d ( だ ). If he was anyone else you'd tell him off for being lazy, but you can't tell off your dad. That's just not right. Hints Picture your lazy dad. Your big, lazy narwhal dad.

meaningMnemonic: Take a helicopter made of leather to the moon to prove your excellent leadership . Some people called you crazy, but you'll show them, as you lead an entire crew of leather helicopter pilots on their first mission to space! Hints Not many people have the leadership it takes to lead such a mission. Imagine what it takes to do it!
readingMnemonic: You've proven your leadership qualities by successfully completing your mission to the moon. " Hah ( は )!" you say to all your haters. "I knew I could do it — that'll teach you! Hah!" Hints Imagine planting your flag on the moon and looking back at everyone who doubted you. You throw your arms up and exclaim, "Hah! I knew I could do it!" The view is breathtaking, but the real thrill comes from showing all your doubters exactly who was right.

meaningMnemonic: Shaving the hair off a geoduck before you try to eat it is absolutely necessary . If you don't, the hair will get caught in your throat and you'll choke. It is necessary that you remove the hair. Hints Picture the page in your cookbook where it says "Shaving the hair off your geoduck = Necessary!!" It's absolutely necessary that you follow that instruction!
readingMnemonic: It is also necessary that you wear a su it ( す ) when eating shaved geoduck. It's a super fancy meal so a suit is necessary for you to enjoy it correctly. Hints What's necessary? To shave the hair off your geoduck and to wear a suit. That's not too hard. You should do it.

meaningMnemonic: If you take a cow 's life you're turning it into an offering . In the old days, cows' lives were given to the gods as offerings pretty often. Hints Picture yourself offering the cow's life up to the god(s). It's a good thing we don't actually have to do this anymore, you think.
readingMnemonic: You prepare the offering with your holy blue sa ber ( せい ). Normally this would be gruesome, but your saber glows and the cow's life shoots up into the sky without you laying a hand on it. Hints Thanks to the mercy of your saber, the offering is quick and painless. A normal saber, however, would have cut that cow to bits. Like, really just wrecked it. Good thing we didn't make you think about that, huh?

meaningMnemonic: If a grain has a fault , it needs to be put back in order . Grains must be perfectly identical at all times, otherwise they'll be thrown out. That's why special people will go out and check them to confirm their regularity . Keeping order is a tough job! Hints Imagine being one of these people who maintain order by going out in the fields and inspecting every single grain, keeping the good ones and plucking off the ones with faults.
readingMnemonic: You can always tell if a company keeps order or if it cheats ( ちつ ) just by looking at the grains. Hints If there are faulty grains in there, they cheated and order was not maintained. Now you have to go through all the grains and throw out the weird ones yourself.

meaningMnemonic: There was once a melon child , that is, a child with the body of a melon. When he was born, his parents didn't want him, so he became an orphan . Hints The "melon boy orphan," is what they called him. Imagine a melon (your favorite kind) with a face and arms and legs sticking out. He walks up to you and says "hello kind person, could you help an orphan?"
readingMnemonic: The orphan melon boy is but a 子 ( こ ). Hints That's the sad thing about the melon orphan boy... he's just a child. "Hello guv, I'm just a child," he says to you.

meaningMnemonic: You think you can catch the soul of the sun in a net without even getting up from your stool ? That's some serious overconfidence , buddy. The fact that you want to stay seated really proves your laziness , too. Hints Imagine the level of overconfidence necessary to think you could capture the soul of such an important celestial body with just a net. Get off your stool, stop being lazy, and go try to catch the soul of something more within your league — a small asteroid, for example.
readingMnemonic: Your overconfidence stems from your man ga ( まん ) addiction, which is also the source of your laziness . You lie in bed for hours a day reading manga and imagining yourself as the protagonist, and it's seriously distorted your sense of reality. This is probably why you think you can do outlandish things like capturing the sun's soul. Hints Manga has also given you the overconfidence to believe that your lack of progress in life isn't due to laziness — it's because you're still in your "training arc."

meaningMnemonic: Under the window , you place a shellfish , then slam the window shut to pierce its tough shell. This is the best way to pierce a member of the shellfish family, I promise. This kanji also has a second meaning. That shellfish you pierced with the window is in two halves now. You can use those halves as plates for sushi. If you count the broken shells you'll know how much sushi you have. That makes them sushi counter s! Hints Imagine the window piercing into the shellfish's shell. Then imagine lining up the pieces, putting sushi on them, and counting them all.
readingMnemonic: Now that your shellfish is properly pierce d and turned into sushi counter s, you can serve them to Genghis Khan ( かん ) and his men. I really hope you counted them correctly too, because there are a lot of them. Hints Carefully count out all the sushi on their pierced shell plates and place them in front of Genghis Khan and his army. As you reach Genghis Khan himself, you realize it's just his ghost, but he's still staring at you as you serve his troops. Ghost or not, you don't want him to pierce you if you mess up.

meaningMnemonic: The rice that's prepared at dawn by the village are provisions for the army. The army is scheduled to arrive right after dawn, so all of the village's provisions for them have to be ready by then. Hints Picture everyone in the village getting all of their rice together as provisions for the army. Even the kids and old people are helping out.
readingMnemonic: Once all of the provisions are ready, the soldiers show up in their row ( りょう ) boats and load it all up. But they aren't done there. "Rice isn't enough, we need roe ( ろう ) so we will have the strength to row our row boats back." And so the village brings them all of their roe too. Hints Picture the soldiers gobbling down their provisions of rice and roe in their row boats as they row away.

meaningMnemonic: If you stand in the wind it will be really quick to knock you over. So quick that you probably won't even know the wind did it. You'll end up standing up only to be knocked over again, just as quick. Hints Imagine how quick the wind knocks you over when you stand up. So quick, you don't even remember being up. Try again and count how many seconds it takes for it to knock you down. Less than one. Now that's quick.
readingMnemonic: That quick wind is quicker than you can say Satsu ki ( さつ ). And "Satsuki" is a pretty quick sounding name already. Go ahead, say "Satsuki" as quick as you can right now. Heck, try it a few times. Hints Okay, pretty quick, but this wind is even quicker than that.

meaningMnemonic: All you need are some flowers , fish , and grain and you've got yourself a potion that can revive just about anyone or anything! Hints Just don't forget the ingredients you'll need: flowers, fish, and grain. Imagine yourself throwing them all into a big cauldron and brewing up a potion powerful enough to revive a person!
readingMnemonic: This potion able to revive any being just has one small downside: it tastes like so ap ( そ ). Hints As long as you can get over the awful taste of soap, this is some good, powerful stuff! And considering this'll be administered to dead things… the taste is probably not so important.

meaningMnemonic: Play your drum under the moon and your hair will swell ! The more you play and the longer it's under the moon, the larger your hair will swell. Hints Have you been suffering from flat, boring hair? Well do I have the swelling treatment you've been looking for!
readingMnemonic: Using this method, your hair swell s so much it looks like a giant bow ling ( ぼう ) ball is sitting on top of your head. It's all round, and well... swollen is probably the only word that fits. Hints Imagine watching your hair swell to the size of a large bowling ball. Imagine never being able to go bowling again because the comparison is too easy for people to make.

meaningMnemonic: Your poor little scooter got a splinter , so make sure to give it extra nice treatment . This can also mean encounter . Makes sense when you think about how you first have to encounter someone before deciding how you're going to treat them! Also, when this means "treatment," note that it doesn't refer to medical treatment, but rather about how you personally treat or receive people. Hints These are tough times for your scooter, so be patient with it. Try to treat it with understanding and care.
readingMnemonic: Give your scooter only the best treatment , so it can feel real goo ooood ( ぐう ). Hints Not just "good", but "gooooood". The long vowel is important here, so try to think of different ways you could make your scooter feel gooooood. Maybe a nice little wash after you’ve removed the splinter will do the trick.

meaningMnemonic: You're especially win ning when you selflessly devote yourself or overcome personal weaknesses. That's what makes it admirable and praiseworthy ! 殊勝 is a formal term often used to describe someone's commendable endurance, sincere attitude, good intentions, or virtuous actions.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: あいつは殊勝な女だったよ。
sentences.english: That's an admirable woman.

meaningMnemonic: If you do not have any ethics you'll probably do something crappy, like commit adultery or infidelity . Usually only unethical people would cheat on their spouse, right? Unlike 浮気 , which can mean cheating in either dating or marriage, 不倫 is strictly adultery in marriage. It sounds way more serious (and has way bigger consequences). Basically, all 不倫 is 浮気 , but not all 浮気 is 不倫 … Both are bad, but one may come with legal fees.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: どうやら妻が不倫をしているようなんです。
sentences.english: It seems that my wife is committing adultery.

meaningMnemonic: All the art, music, or books that come out after a person die s are considered to be released after death or posthumously .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 没後50年を記念した展覧会を予定しています。
sentences.english: A commemoration exhibition is planned 50 years after their death.

meaningMnemonic: If you have the leadership spirit it means you have a lot of ambition to go after the things you want. And you'll be able to lead others because of it.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: うちの息子は、若いのに覇気が無い。
sentences.english: Despite his youth, my son lacks ambition.

meaningMnemonic: Animals exit the mountains into your land and never seem to die ! They end up appearing frequently in your garden, eating all your yummy carrots and watermelons, and then make their exit back into the hills. They're infesting your home now and you don't know what to do!
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 日本各地でクマが大量出没している。
sentences.english: Bears appear frequently in large quantities all over Japan.

meaningMnemonic: This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. The kanji is aromatic , so this also means aromatic or fragrant . 芳しい is a formal word, often used in writing to describe sweet-smelling flowers, tea, or incense. In a figurative sense it can mean "favorable," too, but this meaning mostly appears in the negative form 芳しくない (unfavorable, poorly received).
readingMnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn this reading yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you: If you want to smell an aromatic fragrance, just open some potpourri. But be careful if it's a can. Fragrant can s will baa ( かんば ) like a sheep at you when you open them. That can baa is just a sweet smell side effect.

sentences.japanese: この季節は、梅の香りがとても芳しいですね。
sentences.english: The plums' aroma is really fragrant during this season.

meaningMnemonic: This is a design from Ayano . Do you know an Ayano who's good at designing things? A couple creative Ayanos include traditional Okinawan folk singer and sanshin player Uema Ayano ( 上間 綾乃 ), and author Takeda Ayano ( 武田 綾乃 ) who won the Yoshikawa Eiji Literary Newcomer Award in 2021.
readingMnemonic: This name uses the readings that you learned with the kanji, so you should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 子供の頃、綾乃というとても無邪気な女の子と友達だった。
sentences.english: When I was a child, I was friends with a very innocent girl called Ayano.

sentences.japanese: 先日、綾乃さんから電話があったんですが、留守電にメッセージが入っていなかったんです。
sentences.english: Ayano called the other day but she didn't leave a voicemail message.

sentences.japanese: 綾乃ちゃんと亮平君が殴り合いをしているけど、どうしよう。
sentences.english: Ayano-chan and Ryohei-kun are having a fistfight, but what should I do?

meaningMnemonic: You embrace someone to keep them stand ing. You're backing and supporting this person, so no matter what happens you've gotta keep them on their feet. 擁立 is a formal word for backing someone up for a position, usually in politics or organizations. It's used when people unite to promote or nominate someone as a leader or as a political candidate.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.
